seasonReviews.outcome: You finished 6th of 6 in the round robin and missed the playoffs. Your season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: The Stamina Checkers endured a brutal 0-5 season, finishing at the bottom of the round robin and missing the playoffs entirely after going all-in on a rigid rain archetype that failed to adapt to weather wars, Trick Room, and grass checks.
seasonReviews.didWell: We successfully constructed a potent core featuring elite rain abusers like Mega Swampert and Basculegion alongside defensive anchors Archaludon and Tsareena, consistently executing our primary offensive plan. Our strategic vision for the draft correctly identified top-tier Swift Swim synergy and priority-blocking utilities to protect our sweepers.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: We committed too heavily to a single-weather style without securing independent alternative win-conditions or speed control options outside of Drizzle, leaving us completely exposed when opponents won weather wars or set Trick Room. Furthermore, our free-agency window decision to keep an underperforming, inflexible 10-point rain roster unchanged at 0-3 sealed our elimination.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: We should have dropped dead-weight filler draft picks like Altaria, Audino, and Castform for more versatile neutral attackers or anti-Trick Room support. During the mid-season window, we needed to aggressively swap for non-weather reliant threats or anti-Prankster tech rather than trusting a stagnant 0-3 lineup. We must prioritize flexible secondary modes instead of relying entirely on Pelipper to establish and maintain rain in every single match.

seasonReviews.outcome: You finished 5th of 6 in the round robin and missed the playoffs. Your season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: The Prank Sinatras finished 2-3 in matches and 5-8 in games, missing the playoffs in fifth place. The season was decided by a roster that had excellent support and disruption but lacked reliable answers to sun, Trick Room, spread damage, and opposing priority, followed by several registrations that did not address those exposed holes.
seasonReviews.didWell: Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Maushold, and Mega Blastoise gave the team a coherent Tailwind, redirection, and special-pressure foundation, and the Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Maushold core helped win the week-one rain matchup and the week-five Shadow Tag matchup. Drafting Mega Blastoise was a sound attempt to preserve a powerful Water mode without consuming the roster's Mega slot elsewhere, while Politoed and Paldean Tauros-Aqua were sensible window additions for Charizard, Incineroar, Kingambit, and rain pressure. The week-five registration correctly used Tauros's Fighting pressure, Maushold's redirection, and Politoed's support to win despite the opponent's Gengar and Grimmsnarl threats.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: The draft spent heavily on overlapping special and support infrastructure while leaving no truly dependable answer to Mega Charizard Y, Focus Sash Excadrill, Armor Tail Trick Room, Mega Gardevoir's Hyper Voice, or Palafin's priority; that was a draft result rather than a piloting failure. The window swap from Alolan Ninetales to Politoed improved the Charizard matchup but removed Snow and Aurora Veil without adding a dedicated Trick Room or anti-spread solution, so it did not repair the roster's central problems. In weeks three and four, both 0-2 losses, the six and the leads repeatedly accepted known matchup issues: Gholdengo was exposed to Incineroar plus Kingambit, Taunt was treated as sufficient against Mental Herb Farigiraf, and Mega Blastoise was registered without enough immediate protection or speed support to carry its matchups; week one also failed to leverage Blastoise and let Mega Swampert reach a later Earthquake.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: I would retain Alolan Ninetales at the window, or replace it only with a directly available anti-sun or anti-Trick-Room option, rather than making the Politoed swap solely to improve Mega Blastoise's Water damage. I would register a dedicated Trick Room plan against Aura Borealis, including a way to handle Mental Herb Farigiraf, instead of relying on Whimsicott Taunt and Encore while bringing no alternate speed mode. Against Parting Shot Callers, I would stop defaulting to Gholdengo beside the Incineroar/Kingambit pairing and select a lead built around immediate Fake Out, Intimidate, Protect, and Aura Sphere pressure while preserving Whimsicott for Tailwind and Encore. Against Drought Conditions, I would make Mega Blastoise the centerpiece of an explicit anti-Charizard line and pair it with a plan for Sash Excadrill rather than treating Snow and Aurora Veil as the primary answer.

seasonReviews.outcome: You reached the playoffs as the 2nd seed and were eliminated in the semifinals. Your season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: Aura Borealis finished 3-2, earned the second seed, and reached the semifinals before Drought Conditions eliminated us 2-1. The season succeeded because the Floette/Farigiraf core produced clear winning modes into rain and speed control, but it ended because the same sun-Excadrill matchup that beat us 0-2 in Week 1 remained unresolved in playoffs.
seasonReviews.didWell: The draft correctly identified Mega Floette, Farigiraf, Mega Camerupt, Mega Mawile, Heliolisk, and Tauros as a coherent collection of Fairy offense, Trick Room, anti-priority, rain insurance, and physical mitigation. The Week 2 2-1 win over Perish Trappers was a registration and piloting success: Mental Herb Farigiraf plus Mega Camerupt, with Earth Power rather than spread-move reliance, directly answered Grimmsnarl screens, Bastiodon Wide Guard, and the Gengar/Steel shell. Week 3 and Week 4 were the roster at its best: Floette/Farigiraf, Heliolisk, and the alternate Mawile mode handled Stamina Checkers' Pelipper-Swampert-Basculegion rain and Prank Sinatras' Whimsicott/Gholdengo structures for consecutive 2-0 wins. Keeping the roster through free agency was defensible because those existing modes were proven and no swap obviously replaced Heliolisk's rain role or the multiple-Mega flexibility.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: The biggest season-defining failure was a draft/window problem against Drought Conditions: the roster had no reliably durable answer to Mold Breaker Focus Sash Excadrill's Earthquake endgames while also maintaining pressure on Charizard Y and Venusaur. No-swap became incorrect in retrospect because Week 1 already exposed that exact structural hole, and the unchanged ten returned to lose the playoff rematch 1-2 despite targeted preparation. The playoff registration also repeated too much of the Week 1 framework—Farigiraf, Heliolisk, Camerupt, Mawile, Floette, Tauros—without Liepard's Taunt/Encore disruption or Rotom-Fan's Ground immunity, leaving Excadrill's Sash and Earthquake too easy to accommodate. In Week 5, the 1-2 loss to Parting Shot Callers was partly piloting and planning: the team over-relied on preserving a Farigiraf-Camerupt Trick Room line despite Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge chip and Aqua Cutter pressure, and did not establish sufficiently immediate Samurott pressure.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: After the Week 1 loss, I would use free agency to replace the least essential redundant Mega slot—most plausibly Mega Chandelure—with a Ground-resistant or Ground-immune piece that can pressure Excadrill without depending on Trick Room; retaining all four Mega options was less valuable than repairing that matchup. For the playoff rematch with Drought Conditions, I would register Rotom-Fan over Mega Mawile or Mega Floette so Levitate gives a real Earthquake pivot, then build the game plan around breaking Excadrill's Sash before committing Camerupt or Tauros. Against Parting Shot Callers, I would register and prioritize Liepard alongside Palafin or Floette to Taunt/Encore the Incineroar-Samurott tempo turns, rather than treating Farigiraf's Trick Room as the primary route from turn one.

seasonReviews.outcome: You reached the playoffs as the 4th seed and were eliminated in the semifinals. Your season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: Finished 4th at 2-3 (6-6 in games), reached the playoffs, and were swept 0-2 in the semifinals by Parting Shot Callers; the roster was well-built but I mismanaged my best wincon in the deciding series.
seasonReviews.didWell: The draft core was strong and well-priced: Mega Gengar (pick 4), Garchomp (pick 9), and Grimmsnarl (pick 16) anchored the team, and the value picks Empoleon (pick 28, 7pts), Slowbro (pick 33, 7pts), Lucario (pick 40, 6pts), Rotom-Mow (pick 45, 10pts), and Alakazam (pick 52, 5pts) covered Fairy, Steel, Fighting, and Water at low cost. The free-agency swap of Bastiodon for Mawile was correct: Mawile's Steel/Fairy resist and Intimidate were more useful than redundant Bastiodon and cost nothing. I piloted the two wins cleanly: versus Drought Conditions (week 3, 2-0) I routed Charizard-Y through Gengar and Arcanine while keeping Empoleon and Slowbro as sun-blunted walls, and versus Stamina Checkers (week 4, 2-0) Rotom-Mow's Levitate plus Leaf Storm and Thunderbolt perfectly answered the rain core while Garchomp and Lucario broke Archaludon and Swampert.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: I benched my best wincon in the playoffs: against Parting Shot Callers (lost 0-2, elimination) I left Mega Gengar and Alakazam on the bench despite the post-game note that both would threaten Gardevoir, over-correcting from week 1's lesson to never bring Ghost into their Dark coverage. The double-Intimidate plan (Arcanine plus Mawile) in that same series fed Kingambit's Defiant ability, which raises Attack by two stages whenever a stat is lowered, a registration error the note itself flagged as self-sabotage. In week 1 I registered Mega Gengar into Samurott-Hisui's Ceaseless Edge, which is Dark and super-effective on Ghost, and lost 0-2; in week 5 I brought Empoleon into Tauros-Aqua's Close Combat, which is Fighting and a 2x OHKO on Steel, and Grimmsnarl against a team that wants it benched, losing 1-2. Week 2's 1-2 loss to Aura Borealis exposed a roster gap: I benched Slowbro (my only Trick Room user) and leaned on Bastiodon against a Farigiraf plus Camerupt Trick Room and Imprison core that blanked my Protect-heavy plan.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: In the playoff series versus Parting Shot Callers, register Mega Gengar and Alakazam instead of benching them, because Shadow Ball and Psychic directly threaten Gardevoir and the week-1 Dark-coverage fear was over-applied. Drop one of the two Intimidate users (keep Arcanine, bench Mawile) in any Kingambit or Defiant matchup so I am not handing Kingambit a free +2 Attack via Defiant. In week 1, bench Mega Gengar against Samurott-Hisui's Ceaseless Edge and lead Empoleon, Slowbro, and Arcanine bulk instead of feeding Gengar to Dark STAB. In week 5 versus Prank Sinatras, bench Empoleon (dies to Tauros-Aqua's Close Combat) and Grimmsnarl (a poor lead), and bring Slowbro and Garchomp for bulk plus Taunt on Maushold.

seasonReviews.outcome: You reached the final and lost it. You are the league runner-up and your season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: Drought Conditions finished as league runner-up at 3-2 (6-5), drafting a functional Mega Charizard Y sun team and making the correct mid-season Venusaur-to-Mamoswine swap, but ultimately fell in the final to Parting Shot Callers for the second time because the roster lacked enough offensive firepower and Trick Room resilience to beat that opponent twice.
seasonReviews.didWell: The draft was strong: Mega Charizard Y was the right franchise pick, Excadrill was the team's best and most consistent Pokémon across every series, and the Venusaur → Mamoswine window swap correctly addressed the 4× Ice weakness exposed by the Week 2 loss to The Prank Sinatras. Weavile filled the speed-control and Ice-coverage gap cleanly, and the Week 5 sweep of Stamina Checkers showed the sun + Groundquake + Fire Blast macro game was sound against rain.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: Rotom-Wash was a dead pick in the games that mattered — Choice-locked in Week 3, Wacan Berry in Week 4, and contributing almost nothing in the playoff rounds — and should have been swapped for a Trick Room answer or a second breaker. Toxapex consistently lacked offensive pressure and was passive filler. Noivern and Scizor were benched in multiple series despite having relevant roles (Defog, priority, Fairy coverage), meaning the team often played with fewer than six functional Pokémon. The team had no plan B when sun was disrupted or the opponent's recovery core outlasted weather, which is exactly what both Perish Trappers and Parting Shot Callers exploited.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: Swap Rotom-Wash in the window for a Trick Room-resistant pivot or second wallbreaker — Steelix or Absol would have given the team a better answer to Farigiraf Helping Hand Mawile and the Parting Shot Dragapult pivot. Register Noivern and Scizor in every series instead of leaving them benched, since Noivern's Draco Meteor was the cleanest answer to Dragapult and Archaludon and Scizor's Technician Bullet Punch was a 2× STAB threat on Mega Gardevoir and Mega Floette that was never used. Stop leading with Mega Charizard Y in matchups where it is a predictable sacrifice and use Mamoswine or Weavile as the safer lead, preserving the Mega for mid-game. Give Toxapex an offensive move slot or replace it with Steelix, since Regenerator stall alone never won a series against the offensive teams that defined this league.

seasonReviews.outcome: You won the final. You are the league champion and the season is over.
seasonReviews.summary: A dominant 10-1 championship season built on a hyper-efficient draft core (Incineroar, Kingambit, Dragapult, Talonflame, Mega Gardevoir) and matchup-specific six-Pokémon registrations that exploited every opponent's structural weaknesses; the only blemish was a single game dropped to Trick Room, and the only true wasted resource was Scrafty, who never saw the field.
seasonReviews.didWell: The draft's backbone of Incineroar (18), Kingambit (17), Dragapult (14), Talonflame (15), and Mega Gardevoir (16) formed a self-reinforcing engine of Intimidate cycling, priority Tailwind, natural speed control, and spread Fairy damage that was registered together in 6 of 7 series. Budget picks massively overperformed: Serperior at 5 points was registered every single week and won games against rain (Leaf Storm OHKO on Mega Swampert), sun (snowballed into Toxapex), and Perish Trap (Taunt); Appletun at 1 point was a matchup-winner in both weather series. Weekly registration was surgically precise—Throat Chop Incineroar for Mega Gengar, Infiltrator Dragapult for screens, Chople Berry Samurott-H for Mega Mawile Sucker Punch, and the playoff benching of Appletun for Conkeldurr to answer Drought Conditions' new Mamoswine were all correct reads that turned close matchups into sweeps.
seasonReviews.didPoorly: Scrafty at 3 points was drafted as a 'second Intimidate + second Fake Out' engine piece but was never registered across 7 series—those 3 points were pure dead weight that could have patched the roster's structural lack of a Flying resist or Ground immunity. The only game dropped all season (Week 5 vs. Aura Borealis) came with Talonflame registered into a Trick Room matchup where its own game-plan notes acknowledged 'Tailwind offers little value'; bringing Conkeldurr instead—whose Mach Punch, Wide Guard, and Fighting STAB threatened every Trick Room sweeper—was the missed registration call in an otherwise flawless season. The roster also had no Flying resist and only Talonflame as a Fairy resist, structural holes that went unpunished partly because opponents couldn't keep up with the team's offensive pressure.
seasonReviews.wouldChange: Spend Scrafty's 3 points on a budget Flying-resistant pivot—Rotom (any forme) or even a Kilowattrel—to give the roster a switch-in against the Flying moves nothing on the team could absorb. At the free-agency window, swap Scrafty for a Trick Room-disruption piece (Imprison+TR Gardevoir-lite, or a second Taunt user beyond Serperior) after seeing Aura Borealis's Farigiraf-led Trick Room on scout; staying fully pat at 3-0 was defensible but conservative, and the only series loss came exactly to that matchup. Register Conkeldurr over Talonflame in Week 5 against Aura Borealis's Trick Room, matching the game-plan note that Tailwind was low-value there, and run Kingambit with Defiant instead of Supreme Overlord more aggressively in weeks where opponent Intimidate was scouted rather than defaulting to the late-game burst ability.

roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is the single strongest franchise-building pick on the board. Drought is a warping ability—it powers up all Fire moves by 50%, weakens opposing Water attacks, and enables free Solar Beam coverage—making every future Fire-type addition hit harder. Its 159 base Special Attack under sun is devastating, and Fire/Flying gives excellent neutral coverage. The 20-point price is steep, but in a snake draft the premium Pokémon only get more expensive in opportunity cost if you wait.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: Venusaur is the ideal sun-synergy pick at 13 points. Chlorophyll doubles its Speed in sun, making it a blazing-fast 160-Speed bulky special attacker. Its Grass typing resists Water moves aimed at Mega Charizard Y, directly addressing Charizard Y's biggest defensive vulnerability. It also appreciates the sun you're building around and can run Leech Seed/Giga Drain/Sleep Powder/Sludge Bomb to wear down opponents and pivot.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash at 14 points fills a critical gap: Levitate grants Ground immunity to cover Charizard Y's Electric weakness and handle Ground-types like Garchomp and Excadrill. Its Water/Electric STAB threatens opposing Fire types targeting Venusaur and can pressure Pelipper before it sets Drizzle to ruin our sun. Volt Switch provides crucial momentum in doubles, and 14 points leaves 53 across 7 picks—plenty of room to round out the roster.

roster.name: Toxapex
roster.rationale: Toxapex (8 pts) fills the critical physical wall slot at the lowest cost available. With 152/142 physical/special bulk, Regenerator, and Merciless, it shores up the team's biggest defensive gap while Water/Poison typing adds useful resistances. At only 8 points it leaves 45 points across 6 remaining picks—plenty of budget to still grab speed control and a secondary threat.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: Excadrill fills the critical physical breaker slot on my sun team. Mold Breaker Earthquake hits through Levitate and Water Absorb, Iron Head covers Fairies and Flying types, and Swords Dance lets it snowball. At 13 points it leaves 32 points for 5 remaining flex/speed-control picks. It also checks key threats like Incineroar and opposing Garchomp that other coaches are running.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Noivern (9 pts, 123 Spe) fills the critical speed-control slot—can set Tailwind for the whole team, packs Infiltrator to ignore Sub/Light Screen, and adds Flying/Dragon coverage that the current roster lacks. At 9 points it's extremely efficient and leaves 23 points for four remaining flex picks.

roster.name: Weavile
roster.rationale: Weavile fills the most critical gap on my roster: I have zero Ice-type coverage and no fast revenge killer. Dark/Ice typing lets it threaten Garchomp and Noivern (Dragon), Gardevoir and Farigiraf (Psychic), Talonflame and Pelipper (Flying), plus Kingambit and Incineroar (Dark). At 9 points it leaves 14 for three final picks, and its 125 Speed ensures it can clean up weakened threats before they set up.

roster.name: Scizor
roster.rationale: At 11 points, regular Scizor fits my budget while leaving 3 points for two more picks. It provides critical Fairy and Psychic coverage with Technician-boosted Bullet Punch and U-turn, addressing the biggest remaining weakness on my roster against the many Fairy-type threats in opposing lineups like Grimmsnarl, Clefable, and Mega Gardevoir.

roster.name: Steelix
roster.rationale: Steelix (Steel/Ground, 2 points) is the best available option at its cost. Its massive 200 base Defense and Rock Head/Sturdy/Sheer Force ability make it an outstanding physical wall that pairs perfectly with Toxapex's special bulk to form a robust defensive core. Ground/Steel typing also provides valuable resistances and immunities that round out the team's coverage.

roster.name: Absol
roster.rationale: Absol is the only remaining 1-cost entry that fits my team needs. It provides a dedicated Dark STAB user with Sucker Punch priority and the Pressure ability for stall, complementing Weavile's Ice/Dark coverage while filling a gap in pure Dark-type presence. It was explicitly identified in my previous draft note and remains undrafted.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: With Mega Charizard Y already off the board to our left, anchoring our opening round with Archaludon establishes an elite defensive and offensive core that synergizes brilliantly with weather or redirection. Archaludon's Stamina ability and incredible dual typing provide a premier backbone for VGC doubles, blanking many common physical attackers while threatening massive returns with Flash Cannon or Electro Shot. Naming ourselves the 'Stamina Checkers' nods to both its defining ability and our grinding, attrition-based strategic identity.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Pelipper establishes Drizzle rain instantly, activating Swift Swim sweepers and strengthening Water moves while dampening Fire attacks to protect Archaludon. At 18 points, it leaves us with 63 points for the remaining 8 slots and forms a world-class core with Archaludon.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: With Pelipper setting up Rain, Basculegion is the premier physical Swift Swim abuser, offering devastating Adaptability-boosted Wave Crashes and Ghost STAB. It forms a terrifying offensive core alongside Archaludon while maintaining high speed in rain. This pick immediately locks down the primary rain synergy before opponents can contest it.

roster.name: Mega Swampert
roster.rationale: With Pelipper setting rain and Archaludon holding down defensive utility, adding Mega Swampert gives our rain archetype an explosive Swift Swim physical breaker that cleanly outspeeds and dismantles opposing threats. It synergizes perfectly with our current core, maximizing rain offensive pressure while leaving us 29 points for our remaining 6 picks.

roster.name: Raichu
roster.rationale: Raichu provides vital Lightning Rod redirection to protect our water types from electric attacks, as well as Fake Out support and speed control in rain. At 10 points, it fits perfectly within our remaining budget while rounding out the support core for Archaludon, Pelipper, Basculegion, and Mega Swampert.

roster.name: Tsareena
roster.rationale: We secure Tsareena (11 points) to provide Queenly Majesty priority blocking, preventing opposing Fake Out and priority moves from disrupting our rain sweepers Basculegion and Mega Swampert, while leaving 8 points for our final 4 picks.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: With 8 points remaining for 4 picks, we need to pick extremely cheap Pokémon to complete our roster legally. Altaria costs only 1 point, providing a budget-friendly Dragon/Flying option that fits within our remaining point limit.

roster.name: Feraligatr
roster.rationale: With 7 points left and 3 picks remaining, Feraligatr (3 points) provides another strong physical water attacker that synergizes well with the established rain core. This leaves 4 points for the final two picks while ensuring we cover all required roster spots with legal, cost-compliant selections.

roster.name: Audino
roster.rationale: With 4 points left for 2 picks, we must spend at most 3 points on this pick to save 1 point for the final slot. Audino costs 3 points and provides supportive utility, leaving exactly 1 point for our final draft pick to complete the 10-Pokémon roster.

roster.name: Castform
roster.rationale: With 1 point remaining and 1 pick left, Castform costs exactly 1 point and rounds out our final roster spot. It adds a quirky flexible weather user that synergizes with our rain core if needed while fully utilizing our remaining budget.

roster.name: Paldean Tauros
roster.rationale: Paldean Tauros is the best available 3-point closer: Intimidate adds vital physical mitigation, while its Fighting typing pressures the Dark- and Steel-types that challenge Mega Floette and Mega Chandelure. Its speed and Raging Bull’s screen removal provide practical, matchup-specific utility that the roster otherwise lacks.

draftRoster.name: Mega Floette
draftRoster.rationale: Mega Floette is an exceptional all-purpose franchise piece: Fairy Aura amplifies both its already elite special offense and its partners’ Fairy damage, while 74/87/148 bulk gives it real doubles staying power. Its Fairy typing and 102 base Speed are especially valuable into the Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-heavy cores likely to emerge, and it remains flexible across balance, Tailwind, and Trick Room-adjacent builds.

draftRoster.name: Farigiraf
draftRoster.rationale: Farigiraf gives Mega Floette an excellent partner through Armor Tail anti-priority support and a credible Trick Room mode without forcing the entire roster to be slow. It also supplies valuable Psychic pressure into Poison-types while preserving later picks for Ground- and physical-based Steel answers.

draftRoster.name: Mega Mawile
draftRoster.rationale: Mega Mawile is an exceptional value breaker that directly punishes the Steel-types most likely to answer Mega Floette, while Farigiraf gives it a credible Trick Room mode despite its low Speed. Huge Power also makes it a strong physical win condition that is naturally less reliant on special-oriented counterplay and can be selected instead of Floette as the matchup’s Mega.

draftRoster.name: Mega Camerupt
draftRoster.rationale: Mega Camerupt gives this roster the immediate Fire/Ground breaking power it lacks, while fitting naturally beside Farigiraf’s Trick Room mode. It is an excellent matchup-specific Mega alternative to Floette or Mawile and pressures the Steel-, Fire-, and Electric-types that otherwise constrain the Fairy core.

draftRoster.name: Palafin
draftRoster.rationale: Palafin supplies the roster’s most efficient non-Mega offensive Water option and, crucially, a credible faster-mode piece beside the existing Trick Room shell. It patches the team’s Fire/Ground pressure, gives strong pivoting and endgame potential, and still leaves 26 points for five value picks. Its priority is also much safer to deploy with Farigiraf available to deny opposing priority retaliation.

draftRoster.name: Liepard
draftRoster.rationale: Liepard is the most efficient remaining disruption package: Prankster Taunt, Encore, Thunder Wave, and Fake Out give this roster flexible anti-Trick Room and speed-control tools without committing another Mega slot. Its 8-point cost still leaves enough room to add a Water-immunity pivot and three functional low-cost selections.

draftRoster.name: Heliolisk
draftRoster.rationale: Heliolisk is the cleanest remaining answer to the rain roster: Dry Skin turns Water attacks into healing and pressures Pelipper, Basculegion, and Mega Swampert immediately. It also adds valuable fast disruption and pivoting through Electroweb, Glare, and Volt Switch, complementing Farigiraf’s anti-priority support.

draftRoster.name: Mega Chandelure
draftRoster.rationale: Mega Chandelure is an exceptional 9-point matchup piece: it supplies Trick Room and Imprison pressure, a crucial Fire immunity for Mega Mawile, and a powerful alternate Mega mode alongside Floette, Mawile, and Camerupt. Its Ghost STAB also gives this roster much-needed leverage into opposing Farigiraf, Gholdengo, Dragapult, and Mega Gengar structures.

draftRoster.name: Rotom-Fan
draftRoster.rationale: Rotom-Fan is the best remaining two-point utility piece: it supplies a Ground immunity, a durable Levitate pivot, and Electric pressure into the rain-heavy Pelipper/Basculegion/Mega Swampert roster. Taking it now prevents the two-point teams from denying the most generally useful cheap defensive slot.

draftRoster.name: Paldean Tauros
draftRoster.rationale: Paldean Tauros is the best available 3-point closer: Intimidate adds vital physical mitigation, while its Fighting typing pressures the Dark- and Steel-types that challenge Mega Floette and Mega Chandelure. Its speed and Raging Bull’s screen removal provide practical, matchup-specific utility that the roster otherwise lacks.

teambuilds.rationale: We deploy a potent Rain core led by Pelipper's Drizzle to fuel Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Archaludon against their likely Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Mega Blastoise, and Alolan Ninetales squad. Pelipper sets rain and controls speed with Tailwind and Wide Guard against Blastoise/Ninetales, Mega Swampert leverages Swift Swim to punch through Gholdengo and Tauros, Basculegion obliterates with Adaptability Last Respects or Wave Crash, and Archaludon acts as our sturdy defensive anchor with Stamina and Iron Defense.

We bring a dominant rain core featuring Pelipper to set Drizzle, Mega Swampert and Basculegion-Male as ferocious Swift Swim sweepers, Archaludon as a sturdy defensive anchor and rain abuser with Electro Shot, Raichu for speed control and Lightning Rod support, and Tsareena to block priority and pressure bulky waters/grasses. This lineup heavily out-tempos their physical bruisers like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Conkeldurr while overwhelming their speed tiers under rain.

Whimsicott gives priority Sunny Day to disrupt Pelipper and Swift Swim while also enabling Tailwind speed control. Mega Blastoise and Gholdengo pressure the Water- and Steel-heavy roster from the special side, while Ninetales provides a second weather reset, Aurora Veil, and Freeze-Dry pressure into the rain core. Maushold supplies Friend Guard, Follow Me, and Helping Hand support, and Tauros-Blaze threatens Archaludon and Tsareena with Close Combat and sun-boosted Flare Blitz.

Alolan Ninetales overwrites Drought with snow, enabling Aurora Veil and accurate Blizzard while Freeze-Dry pressures Rotom-Wash and Venusaur. Whimsicott provides Prankster Tailwind, Helping Hand, and Encore support for the fast offensive core of Mega Blastoise, Gholdengo, and Tauros-Blaze. Maushold offers Friend Guard and Follow Me to protect the attackers from Charizard, Excadrill, and opposing priority pressure.

Lead Farigiraf + Camerupt into likely Mega Gengar lines: Mental Herb secures Trick Room through Taunt, and Mega Camerupt's Earth Power cleanly removes Mega Gengar even after Perish Song. Mawile supplies the decisive Garchomp/Grimmsnarl answer under Trick Room, while Liepard, Chandelure, and Scarf Heliolisk provide alternate anti-setup, anti-Trick Room, and fast-pressure modes. Preserve the Mega choice: Camerupt is preferred for the Gengar/Steel core, Mawile for Garchomp-heavy fours, and Chandelure for a Ghost-safe pivot and Imprison mode.

The primary anti-sun line is Farigiraf plus Solar Power Heliolisk: Armor Tail blocks Weavile disruption, while Helping Hand Thunderbolt guarantees the Mega Charizard Y knockout in sun. Farigiraf enables a second mode with Mega Camerupt under Trick Room to punish Venusaur, Scizor, Excadrill, Steelix, and Toxapex; Mega Floette is the alternative Mega when Rotom-Wash, Noivern, or the Dark attackers are the bigger concern. Liepard gives a proactive Taunt lead into Venusaur, while Tauros supplies Intimidate, Rock Slide pressure, and screen removal.

This opponent leans heavily on Fairy-type threats (Mega Floette, Mega Mawile) and special/physical powerhouses like Mega Chandelure and Mega Camerupt. Mega Charizard Y opens with Drought to fuel Venusaur's Chlorophyll, giving us instant Solar Beams and a speed advantage. Scizor's Technician Bullet Punch and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb provide essential SE Fairy coverage. Excadrill with Mold Breaker revenge-kills Electric types and threatens Camerupt with Rock Slide. Toxapex walls Mega Camerupt's Fire/Ground with 4x SE Surf and spreads Toxic to wear down bulky foes. Weavile rounds out the team with Ice Shard priority for Rotom-Fan and Night Slash for Ghost types like Mega Chandelure.

This team is built around Drought sun from Mega Charizard Y, which powers Fire STAB to threaten the opponent's Fairy-types (Whimsicott, Alolan Ninetales) and enables Chlorophyll Venusaur to become the team's speed demon under sun. Rotom-Wash pivots with Volt Switch and provides Electric/Water coverage against Blastoise and Morpeko. Toxapex is the physical wall handling Paldean Tauros while wearing down the field with Liquidation burns and Toxic Spikes. Excadrill with Mold Breaker ignores Intimidate from Tauros and demolishes Gholdengo and Ninetales with super-effective Earthquake and Iron Head while managing hazards. Weavile at raw Speed 192 is the fastest Pokémon on the team, providing Night Slash and Knock Off to pressure Psychic-types and Gholdengo, with Ice Shard for priority revenge.

Opponent's Perish Trap revolves around Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag + Perish Song. Dragapult's Ghost type ignores trapping and outspeeds Gengar with 202 Speed, threatening a Life Orb Shadow Ball OHKO. Kingambit and Samurott-H provide additional Dark-type pressure with Sucker Punch and Sharpness-boosted Ceaseless Edge (spikes break potential Sashes). Incineroar cycles Intimidate and disrupts with Fake Out; Throat Chop locks Gengar out of Perish Song for two turns. Serperior's Taunt shuts down Perish Song and screens while Glare cripples Garchomp and Arcanine. Mega Gardevoir supplies spread Fairy damage and Will-O-Wisp for physical attackers like Garchomp. The plan is to lead Dragapult + Incineroar/Serperior, eliminate or neutralize Gengar early, and clean up with priority and snowballing Contrary boosts.

Opponent brings a dedicated rain core: Pelipper sets Drizzle, Mega Swampert and Basculegion sweep with Swift Swim, Archaludon abuses Electro Shot, Raichu provides Lightning Rod, and Tsareena blocks priority via Queenly Majesty. My plan: Talonflame sets Tailwind to match rain speed (Gale Wings Tailwind targets my side, bypassing Queenly Majesty). Serperior's Contrary Leaf Storm OHKOs Mega Swampert and threatens Basculegion while snowballing. Appletun with Thick Fat walls Water moves from both Swift Swim sweepers and survives Ice Punch. Mega Gardevoir provides Pixilate-boosted spread pressure and Moonblast to threaten Archaludon. Dragapult outspeeds everything naturally and hits Basculegion super-effectively with Shadow Ball. Incineroar cycles Intimidate + Parting Shot to neuter physical Swift Swim attackers. Remove Tsareena early (Talonflame Brave Bird, Dragapult Flamethrower) to unlock priority options.

Opponent leans on Mega Gardevoir's Fairy spread, fast Dragapult, and Dark/Fighting physicals (Kingambit, Incineroar, Conkeldurr). My Steel core (Empoleon + Bastiodon) resists Fairy/Dragon and Bastiodon's Wide Guard blanks spread moves, while Gengar's Shadow Tag traps Gardevoir/Dragapult for the Steels to clean and its Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt remove Gardevoir/Talonflame. Slowbro is my only Fighting resist and walls Conkeldurr behind Leftovers+Regenerator; Arcanine's Intimidate/Snarl/Will-O-Wisp soften everything, and Grimmsnarl's Prankster Taunt/Fake Out/Sucker Punch disrupts setup and Dark users, with Colbur/Chople/Occa berries patching each wall's main weakness.

Opponent is Fairy- and special-attack heavy (Mega Mawile, Mega Floette, Mega Chandelure, Mega Camerupt). Three Steel types (Empoleon, Bastiodon, Lucario) resist Fairy and anchor a defensive core; Gengar is the Shadow Tag special breaker; Grimmsnarl Prankster sets screens/Taunt; Arcanine Intimidate softens physical threats (Mawile, Palafin, Tauros). Bastiodon's Wide Guard blanks spread Ground/Fire from Camerupt and Chandelure, and Empoleon/Lucario resist Camerupt's STABs.

Snow plus Aurora Veil gives the team a durable offensive mode, while Whimsicott supplies priority Tailwind, Helping Hand, and Encore. Gholdengo is especially valuable into the opponent's Parting Shot callers because Good as Gold blocks their status moves, and Mega Blastoise pressures Incineroar, Talonflame, and Samurott with reliable Mega Launcher attacks. Maushold redirects attacks and enables Population Bomb, while Tauros-Blaze provides Intimidate, strong Fighting damage into Kingambit and the Dark-types, and Raging Bull to remove opposing screens or Aurora Veil.

The opponent's Perish Trappers rely on Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag to trap a Pokémon while Grimmsnarl's Prankster screens soften our attackers and fast threats like Alakazam and Garchomp apply pressure. Our answer is immediate offensive tempo: Mega Charizard Y sets permanent sun with Drought, turning Solar Power-boosted Fire Blast into a nuke and making Solar Beam free for Empoleon and Bastiodon. Weavile's Ice Shard provides priority revenge killing, Icicle Crash smashes Garchomp and Bastiodon, and Focus Sash guarantees a hit. Excadrill with Mold Breaker provides irreplaceable coverage — Earthquake OHKOs Bastiodon at 4× and hits through Levitate on Rotom-Mow, while Iron Head smashes Grimmsnarl. Toxapex is the defensive anchor, physically walling Garchomp's attacks with Regenerator and Recover while spreading Toxic Spikes and Haze to punish switches and stop setup. Rotom-Wash pivots safely with Volt Switch, threatens Slowbro and Empoleon with Thunderbolt and Hydro Pump respectively, and can Trick a Choice Scarf onto a wall to cripple it. Venusaur is the endgame cleaner — under Drought, Chlorophyll makes it deceptively fast and Growth pushes SpA to terrifying levels, letting a single Leaf Storm OHKO Empoleon and heavily damage every other opponent.

Opponent builds around Mega Charizard Y's Drought sun plus a Chlorophyll Venusaur, so I anchor on Fire-resistant Water walls (Empoleon, Slowbro) that also answer Venusaur with Psychic, while Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag traps Charizard Y and its sun-immune Thunderbolt (2x) is my cleanest KO after a Nasty Plot. Arcanine supplies Intimidate plus Flare Blitz/Wild Charge to blank Weavile's Ice and burn through Venusaur/Scizor/Steelix, Grimmsnarl sets Prankster screens and Play Rough to wall Dark and crush Weavile/Noivern/Absol/Scizor, and Lucario's Fighting/Steel body-checks Weavile and picks off Excadrill/Steelix. Because sun halves my Water damage, I treat Empoleon/Slowbro as walls and route Charizard Y's removal through Gengar and Arcanine instead.

The Prank Sinatras pack multiple Fairies (Whimsicott, Ninetales-A) and the ever-threatening Gholdengo. I'm bringing triple Fire coverage (Incineroar, Talonflame, Dragapult Fire Blast, Gardevoir Mystical Fire) to torch their Steel and Fairy cores, Kingambit to punish Intimidate with Defiant and clean with Supreme Overlord, Serperior to snowball past Mega Blastoise and Gliscor, and Mega Gardevoir as the special nuke with Icy Wind to one-shot Gliscor. Speed control comes from Talonflame's Gale Wings Tailwind, Serperior's Glare, Gardevoir's Icy Wind, and Dragapult's natural 213. Incineroar holds Passho Berry to survive Mega Blastoise's Water Spout and pivot safely.

We bring a dominant rain core featuring Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion-Male, and Archaludon, backed by Raichu for speed control and redirection/support via Lightning Rod and Fake Out, and Tsareena to block priority and pressure bulky waters or grounds. Pelipper sets Drizzle to empower our swift swimmers and hydro/weather moves, while Mega Swampert and Basculegion shred through their offensive threats like Mega Camerupt, Mega Mawile, and Palafin. Archaludon rounds out the defensive backbone with Dragon Pulse, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, and Protect, holding a Shuca Berry to mitigate ground hits.

This six uses Heliolisk, Floette, and Rotom-Fan to make Pelipper rain and Mega Swampert uncomfortable, while Farigiraf supplies Armor Tail protection and a Trick Room reversal into Swift Swim boards. Mega Floette is the usual damage Mega against rain; Mega Mawile is the alternate when the opponent leans on Archaludon, Altaria, or slower physical pieces. Tauros and pre-Mega Mawile provide crucial Intimidate cycling, with Tauros retaining direct pressure into Archaludon and screens.

We bring a precise rain and speed-control team of Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion-Male, Raichu, Archaludon, and Tsareena, ensuring all EV totals adhere to the strict Champions stat cap of 32 per stat and 66 total. Pelipper sets rain for our Swift Swim sweepers, Raichu provides Fake Out and Lightning Rod absorption, Tsareena shuts down opposing priority, and Archaludon acts as a durable special tank.

Our opponent's roster centers around Drought Charizard-Y and physical sweepers. We deploy Pelipper to win weather control with Drizzle, backed by Swift Swim Mega Swampert and Basculegion to overwhelm them with rain-boosted power. Archaludon, Raichu, and Tsareena round out the team to check Electric and priority threats while maintaining offensive pressure.

Rain plus Tailwind gives Mega Blastoise and Tauros-Aqua strong pressure into Camerupt, Mawile, Chandelure, and the opposing Tauros, while Intimidate and Friend Guard improve positioning against their physical attackers. Whimsicott provides priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore to disrupt Farigiraf-based Trick Room, and Maushold can redirect attacks or punish passive turns with Population Bomb. Gholdengo pressures both Mega Fairies and is protected from their status disruption by Good as Gold.

Farigiraf gives this six a reliable Trick Room axis while Armor Tail suppresses opposing priority from Talonflame, Kingambit, and Dragapult, and Mental Herb keeps that mode live through Taunt. Camerupt is the primary Trick Room Mega into Incineroar/Kingambit structures, while Mawile and Floette provide alternate Mega choices when Steel/Fairy pressure or fast Fairy Aura offense is more valuable. Palafin supplies immediate Fire- and Ground-resistant pressure after its pivot, and Liepard disrupts faster non-Dark leads with Prankster control.

Lead Whimsicott with Maushold or Mega Blastoise to establish Tailwind, deny Perish Song and setup with Prankster Taunt and Encore, and exploit rain-boosted Water Spout pressure. Gholdengo is the principal Shadow Tag-resistant attacker and punishes Grimmsnarl, Mawile, Lucario, and Psychic attackers, while Tauros-Aqua provides Intimidate and immediate pressure into Steel- and Fire-types. Politoed preserves the rain mode and supports the damage dealers with Helping Hand and Icy Wind.

This six leans into their likely rain shell with Dry Skin Heliolisk, Palafin pressure, and Floette’s strong Fairy offense, while Farigiraf reverses Tailwind with Trick Room and blocks opposing priority. Registering all three Mega options preserves the endgame choice: Mega Floette is preferred into rain, Mega Chandelure punishes Gholdengo-centric non-rain boards, and Mega Mawile offers Intimidate before evolving plus physical cleanup. Lead Farigiraf aggressively beside a flexible attacker when Whimsicott speed control is likely, and use Palafin’s Flip Turn to activate Zero to Hero safely.

Dragapult outspeeds everything with 198 Speed and threatens Charizard Y with Life Orb Dragon Darts (47–114%, guaranteed after Fake Out chip). Appletun with Thick Fat walls sun-boosted Fire moves and pressures Rotom-Wash/Excadrill with Apple Acid. Incineroar cycles Intimidate, Fake Outs, and pivots. Serperior snowballs with Contrary Leaf Storm into Rotom-Wash and Toxapex. Kingambit cleans late with Supreme Overlord Black Glasses Sucker Punch. Talonflame's priority Gale Wings Tailwind locks speed control even if Dragapult falls.

Tailwind + Intimidate from Talonflame and Incineroar provides speed control and physical damage mitigation. Mega Gardevoir applies spread fairy pressure with Pixilate Hyper Voice and can snipe special walls with Psyshock. Kingambit with Defiant punishes opposing Intimidate and threatens Farigiraf and the Mega Fairies with its Dark/Steel STABs. Samurott-H offers hazard pressure with Ceaseless Edge and handles Mega Camerupt with Aqua Cutter. Dragapult's unmatched speed and coverage keep Palafin and Chandelure in check.

This opponent runs a Parting Shot pivot strategy with Mega Gardevoir and Dragapult as primary win conditions. Toxapex and Rotom-Wash form a defensive backbone that walls Mega Gardevoir's special attacks, while Scizor's Technician Bullet Punch is 2x super-effective on Mega Gardevoir (Steel vs Fairy) and can OHKO. Absol's Knock Off strips Gardevoirite to revert Mega Gardevoir to base stats, and its Sucker Punch provides priority revenge killing. Noivern outspeeds the field at 192 Speed, threatens Dragapult with Draco Meteor, and provides Defog for hazard control. Excadrill's Mold Breaker Earthquake hits Incineroar, Kingambit, and Conkeldurr without hurting its own Levitate-immune Rotom-Wash partner, while Stealth Rock and Rock Slide provide chip damage and Flying-type coverage.

Stamina Checkers are a rain team built on Pelipper's Drizzle and Swift Swim sweepers (Swampert-Mega, Basculegion), so I load three Water-resists/immunes — Rotom-Mow (Levitate makes it immune to Ground and it resists Water while burning the physical sweepers and OHKOing Swampert with Leaf Storm), Empoleon, and Slowbro — to blunt their Water spam. Garchomp and Lucario break the non-Water threats (Archaludon, Pelipper) with super-effective Ground/Fighting/Rock, and Mega Gengar supplies a Perish Song + Shadow Tag trap plus Ghost damage on Basculegion. Slowbro's Trick Room is my speed-control button to flip the Swift Swim boost back against them.

The opponent's core is a rain setup with Pelipper enabling Swift Swim for Mega Swampert and Basculegion. Charizard-Mega-Y's Drought overrides their rain on Mega Evolution, and Solar Beam OHKOs Mega Swampert at 4x for 162-193%. Fire Blast simultaneously OHKOs Archaludon at 140-166%. Mamoswine's Ground typing gives a free Raichu switch-in (immune to Electric) and Earthquake OHKOs Raichu for 151-179%. Excadrill with Mold Breaker bypasses Archaludon's Stamina, delivering 69-99% with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake. Toxapex walls Basculegion and Feraligatr physically while spreading Toxic Spikes and using Haze to shut down setup attempts. Weavile and Rotom-Wash provide speed control and revenge killing for remaining threats.

Opponent leans on Drizzle rain (Politoed) and Prankster Whimsicott, backed by Steel/Ghost Gholdengo and Water-heavy hitters. Rotom-Mow (Grass/Electric, Levitate) and Empoleon (Steel) soak the rain and resist Fairy, while Garchomp's Ground tears through Gholdengo, Qwilfish, and Morpeko. Mega Gengar's speed and Taunt shut down Whimsicott/Meowstic, Grimmsnarl lays Prankster screens and Fake Out, and Slowbro brings Trick Room plus Psychic/Fighting coverage.

Lead Farigiraf + Heliolisk aggressively into Charizard Y structures: Armor Tail shuts off Weavile’s priority disruption, while Helping Hand Solar Power Thunderbolt cleanly removes Charizard in sun. Farigiraf preserves Trick Room for Mega Camerupt against Excadrill, Scizor, Steelix, Mamoswine, and Toxapex; register all three Mega options so Camerupt, Mawile, or Floette can be selected after seeing their six. Tauros provides Intimidate and Rock Slide pressure, while Mega Floette gives the safer Rotom-Wash/Noivern/Dark-attacker route.

Sun team centered on Mega Charizard Y's Drought to power Fire Blast OHKOs against Fairy threats (guaranteed OHKO on Mega Mawile, possible OHKO on Mega Floette). Excadrill with Focus Sash and Mold Breaker is the anchor revenge killer, delivering 4x super-effective Earthquake to OHKO Mega Camerupt and heavily damage Mega Mawile. Three priority users — Scizor Technician Bullet Punch, Weavile Ice Shard, and Mamoswine Ice Shard — guarantee speed control under Trick Room from Farigiraf and provide clean revenge killing. Scizor's Bullet Punch is also 2x super-effective on Mega Floette via Steel STAB. Rotom-Wash pivots safely with Volt Switch and threatens Mega Chandelure and Mega Camerupt with Hydro Pump. Mamoswine's Thick Fat halves incoming Ice damage, addressing the team's historical Ice weakness, while Earthquake covers Palafin and Mega Mawile.

Rematch vs Perish Trappers (won 2-0 in W1). They'll likely adapt by bringing Garchomp, Rotom-Mow, or Mawile to handle our Dark-types. Dragapult at 209 Speed outspeeds everything and threatens Mega Gengar with Life Orb Shadow Ball (65–150%) and Garchomp with Draco Meteor (88–196%). Incineroar's Throat Chop locks Gengar out of Perish Song for 2 turns while cycling Intimidate. Kingambit's Defiant punishes Arcanine/Mawile Intimidate and Black Glasses Kowtow Cleave nearly guarantees the OHKO on Gengar. Mega Gardevoir spreads Pixilate Hyper Voice and burns physical attackers. Serperior's Taunt shuts down Perish Song and Prankster Grimmsnarl; Glare cripples fast threats. Samurott-H stacks Ceaseless Edge Spikes (no removal on their team) and Sharpness Aqua Cutter threatens Arcanine/Garchomp. Lead Dragapult + Incineroar or Serperior to neutralize Gengar early, then clean with priority and snowballing Contrary boosts.

Opponent is Dark/Fighting-physical heavy with Mega Gardevoir as the special wincon and an Incineroar+Dragapult pivot lead that U-turns/Parting Shots for tempo. I lead twin Intimidate (Arcanine + Mawile) to blunt their physical core and back it with Grimmsnarl's Prankster screens and Taunt to stop Serperior/Samurott setup. Empoleon (Chople) and Slowbro (Leftovers) wall Gardevoir and the Fighting-types, while Garchomp's Ground/Rock/Dragon coverage and Slowbro's Focus Blast clean up Kingambit and Talonflame. Per the week-1 lesson I bench Mega Gengar — their Dark coverage (Samurott Ceaseless Edge, Scrafty, Incineroar) punishes Ghost — and answer Gardevoir with my Steel/Fairy core instead.

This opponent's Parting Shot core (Mega Gardevoir, Dragapult, Incineroar) relies on constant pivoting and speed advantage. Our answer is overwhelming priority and fast offense: three Ice Shard/Bullet Punch users (Scizor, Weavile, Mamoswine) guarantee we act first even under Trick Room, Noivern's Draco Meteor OHKOs Dragapult, and Excadrill's Mold Breaker Earthquake hits Incineroar/Kingambit/Conkeldurr without fear of Intimidate. Toxapex is the defensive anchor, stalling physical attackers and spreading Toxic Spikes to punish every Parting Shot pivot.

Rematch vs Drought Conditions (won 2-0 W4). They'll likely bring new Ice threats Weavile/Mamoswine to answer my W4 Appletun/Serperior/Dragapult. I'm dropping Appletun for Conkeldurr, whose Sheer Force Close Combat and Mach Punch destroy both Ice-types and Excadrill. Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds Weavile and threatens Charizard-Y with Life Orb Dragon Darts, plus Fire Blast for Scizor/Steelix. Incineroar cycles Intimidate and Fake Outs; Kingambit cleans with Supreme Overlord and is Toxic Spikes immune; Talonflame sets priority Tailwind and Taunts Toxapex; Serperior snowballs Contrary Leaf Storm into Rotom-Wash/Mamoswine while spreading Glare. Lead Dragapult + Incineroar or Talonflame + Incineroar to seize speed control and pressure early.
